Subject: Pilot costs and commit-linked credits for Nebula Health

Hi Marcus / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Nebula is excited to validate the integration with a 6-week pilot, but procurement asked me to clarify how Redwood handles pilot credits and how those credits tie to any subsequent commit. High-level asks: 

- How many free credits do you typically provide for a pilot of this scope (we expect ~10M tokens across models)?
- If we convert to a committed usage contract, how do pilot credits interplay with committed credits (do they net out, expire, or convert to launch credits)?
- What are the slab/volume discount mechanics on the hosted API per-token pricing for commit tiers (we need example math for budgeting)?

Attached: Nebula NDA (signed) and a short procurement questionnaire — they asked for sample pricing and a sample term sheet. Can you send a starter term sheet we can share with legal?

Appreciate a quick cadence — procurement needs rough numbers by end of week to keep the calendar moving.

Best,
Emily Zhao
Head of Product Integrations
Nebula Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Pilot costs and commit-linked credits for Nebula Health

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the NDA.

Quick reply with a starter outline (will follow with a formal term sheet PDF):

- Pilot proposal: 6 weeks, up to 10M tokens of hosted API usage as complimentary credits. Credits valid for usage during the pilot window only and expire at pilot end (we can discuss extending if conversion is delayed).
- Commit conversion: If Nebula signs a 12-month commit within 30 days of pilot end, we offer an industry-standard conversion: pilot credits applied against first 30 days of billed usage and an additional launch credit equal to 10% of the committed annual spend (applied as monthly billing credits).
- Tiered per-token pricing (example):
  * No commit: $0.0009 / token standard host rate
  * 100M token annual commit: $0.00075 / token (17% discount)
  * 250M token annual commit: $0.00062 / token (31% discount)
  * Above 500M: custom pricing + volume rebate to achieve ~40% effective discount depending on model mix
- Risk-sharing: we can structure a partial giveback if actual usage is <50% of commit over the first 6 months; propose a graduated clawback schedule (detail in term sheet).

I'll attach a quick term sheet PDF (pilot_credit_term_sheet.pdf) with these numbers and an example earnout schedule. Suggest a 30-minute call Friday to walk legal through the conversion mechanics.

Marcus
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pilot_credit_term_sheet.pdf

Looping in a couple of operational clarifications from the product/ops side: 

- Credits scope: Pilot credits are limited to Hosted API endpoints (not Dedicated capacity). If Nebula later requests a Dedicated deployment we treat pilot credits as a one-time launch concession subject to an open ticket to migrate capacity.
- Billing granularity: We bill per-token with hourly aggregation. For rebate calculations we use monthly usage buckets.
- Suggested compromise: smaller up-front pilot credits (8M instead of 10M) + an after-the-fact usage rebate that pays out over the first quarter after committing (this reduces potential giveback risk while leaving enough runway for Nebula to validate).

I'll be on the Friday call to cover operational handoffs and any KV-cache / batching considerations that affect cost curves.

—Laura
Head of Customer Success Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-18T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Nebula pricing — suggested redlines

Forwarding suggested legal/finance redlines for the pilot + commit construct. Key asks in the redline doc (redlines_terms_v1.docx):

- Define "token" and billing granularity explicitly (tokens measured per API call, rounding rules).
- Pilot credit escrow: escrow the pilot credit value and apply to first-use only; if Nebula does not sign a commit within 60 days post-pilot, remaining escrow is forfeited (minimizes credit abuse).
- Clawback cap: propose max clawback = 30% of credits (vs procurement's 25%). We should be firm on a slightly higher cap if we accept larger upfront credits.
- Migration to Dedicated: if Nebula migrates to a Dedicated deployment within 12 months, any unspent pilot credits may be applied toward the first month of Dedicated billing up to 50% of the remaining credit balance.

I recommend we push back on a hard 25% cap; 30% gives us margin while still appearing concessionary.

—Rishi
Head of Pricing Strategy
Redwood Inference

- Concrete commit tiers and per-token rates: No commit $0.0009, 100M = $0.00074, 250M = $0.00061 (we tightened pricing slightly after internal review).
